<description>
The mempool fee rate estimator can't always return an estimate:

i)   right after first startup (or after re-syncing through IBD) it hasn't tracked
     enough recent blocks yet;
ii)  the mempool is empty or too sparse to fill the requested block percentile,
     e.g. after a cold restart with persistence off or a missing/corrupt
     mempool.dat.
iii) recent blocks cover too little of the mempool (low coverage); and
iv)  the mempool is still loading.

Previously, case (ii) with a healthy mempool will returned the fee rate
floor (the higher of the minimum relay fee and the current mempool minimum fee).
This can be a significant underestimation, since the now-missing mempool may have
held much higher-feerate transactions. The remaining cases surfaced the mempool
error directly from the combined estimate.

This PR makes the combined estimate (`estimatesmartfee` with
`fee_rate_estimator=none`, the default) fall back to the block policy estimate
whenever the mempool estimator isn't ready, instead of returning the floor or
surfacing the error:

- The mempool estimator now returns an error instead of flooring an unfilled
  percentile, so an empty/sparse mempool is treated like any other not-ready
  state rather than potentially silently underestimating.
- The combined estimate starts from the block policy estimate and only lowers it
  with the mempool estimate when one is available. An error is returned only when
  the block policy estimate itself is unavailable.
- Calling `estimatesmartfee` with `fee_rate_estimator=mempool_policy` explicitly
  still returns the failure.

When the mempool fails to load at startup (persistence off, or a missing/corrupt
mempool.dat), init notifies the estimator, which clears its tracked mined-block
window. Otherwise the estimator would keep a window describing a mempool the node
no longer has; clearing it makes the estimator report insufficient data until the
window refills from the current tip, so the combined estimate falls back to block
policy meanwhile.

This is an alternative to #36095.
</description>

- resolved concerns: Ensured combined mode falls back to block policy on both low coverage and insufficient data errors rather than surfacing errors.
- resolved concerns: Updated init to avoid treating shutdown-interrupted mempool loads as load failures.

[2026-09-23] rc:4077866617 inline on src/policy/fees/estimator_man.cpp by l0rinc (member):
An AI-assisted review flagged a possible gap here: if the block-policy estimator has no result, this returns an error even when the mempool estimator can provide a fee rate. I put a small test and proposed change in https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/300.

Could you check whether this PR should cover that case too? I’m not sure using the mempool estimate alone is always right, since it can return the relay floor.
[2026-09-23] rc:4083688625 inline on src/policy/fees/estimator_man.cpp by ismaelsadeeq (member):
This is the desired behaviour, it's a belt-and-suspenders on `mempool_policy` fee rate estimator, when we are not seeing txs confirming enough for block policy to provide an estimate, we also should not rely on mempool policy.
[2026-09-23] rc:4083689691 inline on src/policy/fees/mempool_estimator.cpp by ismaelsadeeq (member) (edited 2026-09-23):
Hmm, Good catch. The warm-up in the last commit of this PR attempts to prevent serving the floor in those cases.

The state machine seems to blow-up and this approach is not able to handle all cases, ur diff also only handles during ibd, after ibd u will return flow incorrectly because u do not have the backlog of mempool txs like long running nodes.
So I simplify by disallowing the fee rate return flow completely; this is simpler and should handle the most important likely case of underpaying because I'd assume nodes frequently shut down. But having empty mempool usually occurs in test network. And returning block policy in this case won't hurt much because it will also be on the low end.
[2026-09-23] rc:4083910745 inline on src/policy/fees/mempool_estimator.h by ismaelsadeeq (member):
This is gone now.
[2026-09-23] c:5797758870 comment by ismaelsadeeq (member):
Forced pushed [651b0a9db877..86ef5cc277](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/352283bffbe7ca0b684767baf3ff651b0a9db877..86ef5cc27782ee7b51394753065c1d23215268a4)

- The main change is that I simplified the fix: The mempool estimator now returns an error instead of the relay floor when it can't fill a percentile, and the combined estimate falls back to `block_policy`; hence, an explicit `mempool_policy` query still returns an error in that case. This should handle the most likely case of underpaying because nodes do frequently restart. But having a completely empty mempool on mainnet is rare, it usually occurs in test networks. And returning a block policy in this case won't hurt because it will also be on the low end or an insufficient data error, so users can explicitly pass the relay floor or use the fallbackfee feature in the wallet.

[2026-09-23] c:5801630232 comment by stickies-v (member):
Approach ACK. I was feeling very uneasy about the amount of complexity (process flow more so than code) being tacked on in the state prior to the latest force-push (352283bffbe7ca0b684767baf3ff651b0a9db877..86ef5cc27782ee7b51394753065c1d23215268a4). I think the current approach of simply erroring (and falling back to block policy) whenever the mempool seems like it can't produce an estimate is the best choice for this backport. Solving the biggest problem with the least amount of complexity.

There are now a few quirks with empty percentiles never resulting in a mempool estimate, but I think their impact is limited enough that this remains a good approach. Some quirks:
- economical estimate can end up a higher feerate than conservative (if p50 has a result, but p75 doesn't, the mempool estimate is used for conservative and the block policy estimate for economical)
- as the mempool continually clears until it is almost fully empty, estimated fees will suddenly jump as p50/p75 become empty, the severity depending on how quickly the mempool clears/fees have changed.

I would prefer addressing these in a follow-up where we have less time pressure to find a good solution.

nit: the message of 247d47017f still says the change is necessary for "the warmup fallback", which is no longer part of this PR.
[2026-09-23] rc:4088236014 inline on src/policy/fees/mempool_estimator.cpp by davidgumberg (member):
https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36182/changes/86ef5cc27782ee7b51394753065c1d23215268a4 (_fees: return an error instead of a floored mempool fee rate estimate_)

In the case of a node with a healthy view of the mempool, but a mempool that has less than a p50 or p75 of transactions, don't we actually want to return the floored estimate instead of falling back to the block policy estimator. Not frequent but from looking at the mempool.space chart it has happened as recently as February of this year on mainnet:

And I also imagine this will in practice make the mempool estimator never engage on testnet/signet.

Question: why can't we just rely on the mempool health metrics here?

What are the odds that someone loads a mempool.dat that happens to do a good job matching the catch-up blocks during loading and that someone asks for a fee estimate during that time? And the current approach will only stop the fee estimate if that happens and at the same time the mempool happens to be kind of empty around the time the fee is being requested which isn't necessarily the case.

I wonder if maybe a check should be added to `GetMempoolHealth()` that the current tip height is close to the best known header or something like that but I'll have to look closer tomorrow.
